title: sync --to-store compares the parsed model of both sides, so a lossy parser reports agreement with its own output and the repair never runs
body:
`sync --to-store` decides whether the store and the extract agree by comparing the PARSED MODEL of each side. When the parser is the lossy component, both sides parse to the same wrong value, the verb reports agreement, writes nothing, and exits 0 -- **so the one operation that could repair a parse defect is the operation that cannot see it.**

**Measured in Lamplight, 2026-08-28, on ST0300, behind a store backup copied outside the prune path.** Reported from a consumer estate: the repair this blocked is Lamplight's, the mechanism is Intent's.

## Reproduction

The store holds a truncated citation. The extract on disk holds the whole one:

    store:  '[apps/lamplight/test/lamplight/runner/view_test.exs "here'
    disk:   AT-01.4 [apps/lamplight/test/lamplight/runner/view_test.exs "here -- room-occupancy
            passthrough" :: both doors (from_digest + from_wire) converge on the same primitive
            with alive: false riding the clear entry and the silhouette bare] -- covers AC-01.3
            -- status: green

They differ by 180 characters. The truncation is a known migrator defect, fixed in `e935734d` -- the porter read an AT bracket citation to the first ` -- ` rather than to its closing bracket, and a v2 bracket citation routinely contains one.

Then:

    $ intent sync --to-store ST0300
    note: the store and the extract agree; this restore overwrites nothing
    ok: store replaced from the extract, 1 thread(s)
    $ echo $?
    0

The store is unchanged afterwards, byte for byte. Two lines, and they contradict each other: the first says nothing was written, the second says the store was replaced.

## Why it says they agree

The comparison runs on the parsed model rather than on the stored text. The disk text is parsed by the same component that produced the store's value, so it produces that value again, and the two sides match. **The verb is comparing the parser's output to the parser's output.**

That is a sound design when the parser is trusted, and this is exactly the case where it is not: the reason someone reaches for `--to-store` is that the store is suspected wrong.

## Why this is not simply the porter defect

The fix commits `e935734d` and `eff618e8` are both ancestors of the binary under test (`b4d63b44`, sha `1dd65db8`), so the repair logic is present. But those are `fix(port)` -- the **v2 migration** path -- and on an already-migrated estate no available verb runs it:

- `ingest --from-md` on a migrated estate is a parse check that writes nothing at rc 0 -- **issue 0097**, and this is the second verb in that family to return 0 for "did nothing".
- `sync --to-store` is the subject of this issue.

So an estate carrying migrator damage has an intact extract on disk, a fixed migrator in its binary, and **no route between them.** In Lamplight that is 74 rows across ten threads, all ten realised on disk, with a full pre-cut tree also available in git.

## What would fix it

The narrow repair is to compare the RAW STORED TEXT of the extract against the raw stored text of the store, and let the parse happen only on the write path. A round-trip that normalises both sides through the suspect component cannot detect a fault in that component.

Failing that, the message must stop claiming agreement it has not established. **"The parsed forms match" is a different sentence from "the store and the extract agree",** and only the first one is true here.

A separate, smaller thing: `note: ... overwrites nothing` and `ok: store replaced from the extract, 1 thread(s)` should not both print. The second reads as the operation having happened.

## Not claimed

I have not read the comparison's implementation; the mechanism above is inferred from the observable behaviour -- identical inputs on the two sides differing by 180 characters, reported as agreeing -- and from `e935734d`'s own description of the parse. **A one-line probe at the comparison site settles whether it is a model comparison or a digest over a normalised form.** The distinction does not change the effect.

**Practice this is an instance of: a verb whose job is to repair a suspected fault must not use the suspect component to decide whether repair is needed.** The check and the thing being checked have to be independent, or the check inherits the fault and reports health.
